title: I wanted the lab to feel like a place where a little chaos is part of the fun.
author: DigitizedMagic
selftext:
Hey, I’m Danny! I made Chemtris for anyone who sits down for a quick round and ends up spending the evening chasing a high score. My favorite part is when you pull off a move you wouldn’t even have spotted a few runs ago.

I wanted it to look like an old arcade machine from some eccentric scientist’s basement. I used AI to explore the 2D art, then picked and edited the pieces around a few things I kept coming back to: brass, blue-green enamel, and thick glass. The fun design challenge was making the lab light up without losing track of the board. I also used AI for the title-screen music and Steam artwork.

For anyone here who’s used AI for game art, what helped you make assets from different generations feel like they belonged in the same game?

Chemtris hits Steam Early Access tomorrow, November 25. If it looks like your kind of “one more run” game, a wishlist would make my day.
